alt: Assignment A is 30 marks: 12 for AO1 and 18 for AO2, which is 60%. It uses three Anthology Part 2 texts including at least one poem and one prose text, one focus such as setting, character, event or theme, and about 1200 words. The suggested task asks how the writers use language and structure to present the focus in the three texts.
caption: Three texts, one focus, about 1200 words; AO2 carries 60% of the marks.

after: ## Choosing a trio and a focus
alt: Three tests for a focus: is it central in each text, do the writers present it differently, and do the texts use different methods? Weak focuses are improved: “Feelings” becomes “Moments of private realisation”, “War” becomes “Violence and its aftermath”, and “Women” becomes “The pressure of other people’s expectations”.
caption: A good focus is narrow enough to argue and broad enough for all three texts.

alt: A table of levels 3 to 5. AO1 runs from “clear and relevant selection” at Level 3 (7–9) to “perceptive interpretation” at Level 4 (10–12), its top level. AO2 runs from “clear explanations” at Level 3 (7–10) through “detailed exploration” at Level 4 (11–14) to “perceptive analysis” at Level 5 (15–18).
caption: The top levels reward perceptive interpretation and analysis.

alt: Two essay structures. Integrated by idea: each paragraph takes one aspect and discusses two or three texts within it. Sequenced with links: one section per text, each linking back to the previous one and pointing forward. Either opens with a thesis and closes with a judgement about what the three texts suggest together.
caption: Integrated or sequenced, the essay needs a thesis and links throughout.

alt: A plan grid for the trio “The Bright Lights of Sarajevo”, “Significant Cigarettes” and “An Unknown Girl”. Paragraphs cover setting as threat, how the meeting is shaped, identity, and endings: hope in Harrison, uncertainty in Tremain and something that will fade in Alvi. The conclusion presents the encounters as fragile but meaningful.
caption: Plan by idea so every paragraph compares the three texts.

alt: Four stages: you write the draft independently, the teacher may suggest general improvements, you make the corrections, and once marked the work must not be rewritten. The draft stage has three jobs: check every paragraph answers the focus, replace retelling with analysis, and include close reading in each text.
caption: The teacher may advise; you make every change, before marking.
